title: Evaluate the answer
summary: Check an AI answer against supplied evidence and reject unsupported claims.

scenario.briefing: An AI assistant answered a question about the campus refund policy using two supplied documents. Check whether every claim is supported and decide whether to act on it.

objectives.description: Identify claims not supported by the sources.

hints: Compare each sentence with the source text.
The 30-day window is stated. The 14-day exception is not in the sources.
A confident answer can still contain invented details.
Reject the answer until the 14-day exception is removed or a source is supplied.

misconceptions.description: Accepting a confident, detailed answer without source support.
misconceptions.feedback: Specific wording is not evidence. The exception claim has no cited support, so the answer must be rejected or corrected.

misconceptions.description: Treating fluent prose as proof of correctness.
misconceptions.feedback: Fluency measures style. Correctness needs source support, tests, or an explicit rubric.

sections.title: Ground claims in evidence
sections.body: An answer is only as trustworthy as its support. For factual questions, compare each material claim with the supplied sources. A missing citation is not automatically false, but it is unverified and must be treated that way.

sections.title: Evaluate the task, not the style
sections.body: Use a rubric: correctness, completeness, support, and constraints. Run tests or check sources independently. Do not let confident tone or specific numbers substitute for evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Supporting an answer with trusted evidence.
A fluent but unsupported or false generated claim.

steps.title: Review the answer
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.

artifact.title: AI answer with sources
artifact.caption: Sources supplied with the question.
artifact.content:
Sources:
1. Refunds are available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.
2. Opened software is refundable only if it is faulty.

AI answer:
"You can request a refund within 30 days with a receipt. Opened software is refundable only if faulty. There is also a 14-day exception for campus clubs, and the refund is always approved immediately."

Confidence: high.

findings.label: The 14-day club exception is not supported by either source.
Immediate approval is not supported by either source.
The 30-day receipt rule is supported by source 1.
The faulty-software rule is supported by source 2.
High confidence makes the unsupported claims acceptable.

verdicts.label: Remove unsupported claims or supply sources before using the answer
Shorten the answer without checking claims

steps.explanation: Two supported facts are correct, but the exception and immediate approval are invented. Confidence is not evidence.
hints: Check each claim against the cited source, not the tone of the answer.
Look for a claim the sources do not support.
A confident answer can still be wrong.
Reject the answer: the unsupported exception claim remains, whatever its style.

steps.title: Reliable evaluation

statements.label: Material claims should be checked against trusted sources.
For code, executable tests provide independent evidence.
A rubric makes evaluation more consistent.

steps.explanation: Evaluation compares output with evidence and explicit criteria. Style is not correctness.
hints: Evaluation needs a source of truth.
A rubric makes criteria explicit and repeatable.
Fluency is not evidence of correctness.
Select source support, tests, and rubric; reject fluency as proof.

accessibility.summary: Sources and answer are plain text. Findings and verdict use labeled controls.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Space for findings and arrow keys for the verdict.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Source numbers are announced so claims can be compared with evidence.
